title: "refactor: Let the system-host template own the contracts decision"
type: refactor
status: active
date: 2026-02-10
---

# refactor: Let the system-host template own the contracts decision

**Repos involved:** this repo (`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`) and the template library
(`integrio-intropy/intropy-templates`). The library is fetched per release tag at
scaffold time (`internal/template/library.go`), so the two sides must ship in
dependency order (Phase 1 then Phase 2) and the CLI release notes must name the
minimum template release.

---

## Overview

`sys create` currently fails any workspace that has component scaffolds but no
`shared-library` scaffold with "no shared contracts project found …"
(`internal/system/assemble.go:100`). That rejects a perfectly valid shape — a
host with only transactional integrations has neither topics nor contracts —
and it encodes a template-level decision ("every host references a contracts
project") in the CLI. This plan moves the contracts decision to where the
package doc says it belongs: the CLI keeps workspace knowledge, the template
library owns all generated content.

Two changes, in dependency order:

1. **CLI** — pass raw workspace facts only (names, kinds, wiring, the detected
   contracts sibling path when one exists) and stop requiring a shared library
   when the system has no topics. Drop the CLI-computed C# field identifiers
   (`pascalIdent`) and the csproj `include` path from the payload.
2. **Template library** — make `sharedContracts` optional in the system-host
   manifest, declare a conditional dependency on the shared-library template
   for topic-bearing systems, and derive field identifiers / the
   `ProjectReference` include path in the templates.

---

## Problem Frame

A user running `sys create` in a workspace holding only transactional
integrations (e.g. `domains/orders/trans`) gets:

```
error: no shared contracts project found (template role "shared-library"): Topics.cs needs the contract types
```

But a transactional-only system has `Topics == []`, so the rendered
`Topics.cs` carries no `TopicRef<T>` and needs no contracts namespace. The
guard fires because `Assemble` requires `len(shared) >= 1` unconditionally
(`internal/system/assemble.go:99-104`), and `buildPayload` unconditionally
computes a `ProjectReference` path into the payload
(`internal/system/payload.go:60-65`). Beyond the bug, the CLI currently owns
three template decisions:

- (a) whether a host must reference a contracts project,
- (b) the C# field identifiers in `Topics.cs` / `Connectors.cs`

content.text:
## Analysis: tests, template fixtures, and the CLI↔template boundary

### How the test layers are organised

The test suite actually has a deliberate three-tier structure for the template boundary:

1. **Pure engine tests** (`internal/template/*_test.go`) — render, resolve, dependencies, archives. No knowledge of *what* any real template contains. Clean.
2. **Fixture-backed behavior tests** (`internal/system/create_test.go`, `internal/deploy/manifests_engine_integration_test.go`) — drive the full command through `httptest`, but with hand-written "trimmed but faithful copies" of the real templates inline as Go constants.
3. **Real-template gates** — `internal/system/real_template_e2e_test.go` (tag `e2e`) and `internal/deploy/localtemplates_test.go` (tag `integration`), both gated on `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR` pointing at a local `intropy-templates` checkout.

So the layering idea is sound. The problems are in tier 2 and the reachability of tier 3.

### Problem 1: tier 2 fixtures re-implement template logic in the test file

`internal/system/create_test.go` contains ~200 lines of C# Go-template text (`topicsCSTmpl`, `portsCSTmpl`, `systemClassCSTmpl`, `systemHostCsprojTmpl`) that copy the real template's derivation logic — the `regexReplaceAll "[-._]" ... | title` field-identifier derivations, the topic/port join dictionaries, the conditional csproj reference. The header comments are candid about this: *"trimmed but faithful copy … The projectName/systemClass derivations match the real template."*

That is not mocking at the seam — it is maintaining a second implementation of the template repo inside the CLI's test file. Consequences:

- **The fixture can lie in lockstep with the assertions.** The assertions (`Ports.OrderExtractorSource`, `Topics.Orders`) are checked against output rendered by the fixture, so if both drift from the real template in the same way, the suite stays green while `sys create` produces broken C# against the real library. Nothing in CI can catch that.
- **It will silently rot.** When the real template changes (and the docs/plans show it does — the facts-payload refactor in `docs/plans/2026-02-10-001`), someone must hand-sync the copy. There is no mechanical link.
- **It blurs ownership.** The repo just did a refactor to move field-identifier derivation *out of the CLI and into the template* — and the test file promptly re-embedded that derivation in `create_test.go`. The boundary is respected in production code and violated in test code.

`internal/deploy/manifests_engine_integration_test.go` has the same pattern (fixture `deploy-host`/`deploy-component` templates that "deliberately mirror the real template's shape"), though the mirroring there is shallower — kustomize overlays and `spec.files` conditionality, not a re-implementation of a derivation algorithm.

### Problem 2: the tests that would catch drift don't run in CI

`.github/workflows/test.yaml` runs `-tags integration` but never `e2e`, and never sets `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR`. So:

- `real_template_e2e_test.go` — never executes in CI.
- `localtemplates_test.go` — compiles under `integration` but self-skips without the env var. (The file even warns: Go's test cache doesn't know about the external directory, so you must pass `-count=1` — a sign of a seam the tooling can't see.)

The real-template tests are, by their own comments, "an authoring aid rather than something CI can run." That means the drift-detector exists but is opt-in and manual.

### Problem 3: residual cross-repo knowledge in production code

The segregation is *mostly* good — `payload.go` is a facts-only contract and says so clearly. Two leaks remain:

- `create.go` mirrors sprig's kebab-case conversion via `xstrings.ToKebabCase` with the comment "Exact parity with the templates' `{{ .name | kebabcase }}`". The CLI must predict the template's derivation; if the library changed its filter, the CLI's output dir and the rendered content diverge.
- The version gate `requireFactsPayload` (min `v0.4.0`) and the post-render read-back of `projectName`/`systemClass` from the scaffold record couple the CLI to specific template releases and derived value names. That's inherent to a versioned contract, but it's worth naming: the payload keys and derived value keys *are* the API between repos, and today that API exists only as prose comments plus fixtures.

### Is segregation poor? My verdict

**In production code: no.** The facts-only payload, the version gate, and the package docs ("the template library owns all generated content; this package owns workspace knowledge") show a well-thought-out boundary. The February refactor actively improved it.

**In test code: yes, in one specific place.** `internal/system/create_test.go` is the outlier. It doesn't mock *output* (which would be fine — return canned files, assert CLI wiring); it re-implements the template's *derivation logic*, then asserts on the derivations. Those assertions (`Ports.OrderExtractorSource`, the csproj include path) belong to the template repo's own test suite, not the CLI's.

### Recommendations, in order of leverage

1. **Shrink `create_test.go`'s fixtures to minimal stubs.** The fixture needs a valid `template.yaml` (parameters, `values` derivations for `projectName`/`systemClass` since `Create` reads them back, the `spec.files` `when` conditions, and the dependency declaration) plus skeleton files that *echo* the payload rather than derive from it (e.g. a `Topics.cs.tmpl` of `topics: {{ .topics | toJson }}`). Assert that the CLI assembled the correct payload and wired conditionality — the contract — not that `orders` becomes `Orders`.
2. **Move real-template contract tests to CI.** Check out `intropy-templates` at the pinned minimum release in a workflow job and run `-tags e2e` with `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR` set. That converts `real_template_e2e_test.go` from a manual authoring aid into the drift alarm it's designed to be.
3. **Delete the duplicated-derivation assertions.** `TestRealSystemHostFieldCollisionFails` (asserting on a template-internal error string) and the `Ports.*`/`Topics.*` string assertions test the template's behavior from the wrong repo. Keep one end-to-end smoke assertion; let the template repo own the rest.
4. **Treat the payload schema as a versioned artifact.** A short `docs/` page (or a JSON schema) naming the payload keys, derived value keys, and minimum template release would replace the current "contract by comment" and give both repos one thing to point at.
Are the recommendations understood well enough to implement or should we analyse more?

Mostly yes — the direction is clear and the code is understood. But four decisions/unknowns remain that would shape the implementation. I'd resolve these before writing code rather than analyze further in the abstract:

**1. Where do the derivation assertions ultimately live? (the one real design question)**
Recommendations 1 and 3 remove `Ports.OrderExtractorSource`-style assertions from the CLI repo. Two options:
- **(a)** Drop them here entirely; the template repo owns testing its own derivations (cleanest ownership, but requires the template repo to actually have those tests — unverified).
- **(b)** Keep them only in the CI-gated e2e layer (rec 2), so the CLI repo still alarms on drift.
This decision determines how aggressive the `create_test.go` shrink can be.

**2. CI access to `intropy-templates`**
I haven't verified whether it's a private repo. If it is, the e2e workflow job needs a token with read access, and someone must decide which release tag to pin (the minimum `v0.4.0`, or latest). That's an infrastructure decision, not a code one.

**3. Whether the e2e tests currently pass at all**
`real_template_e2e_test.go` is excluded from CI and opt-in locally. Before building automation on top of it, someone should run it once against a real checkout to confirm it's green — otherwise rec 2 imports a failing test into CI.

**4. Scope guard for the fixture shrink**
`create_test.go` also asserts CLI behavior that must *not* be lost: validation-before-network, the version gate, `--force` semantics, dependency scaffolding. The shrink keeps those and only strips derivation assertions — but `payload_test.go`/`assemble_test.go` should be confirmed to cover the payload shape before the rendered-output assertions come out. Gap 3 is now closed — with a finding that matters more than anything in the original analysis.

## Finding: the real-template gates are red against the current library

**`internal/system` e2e tests** (run locally with `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR`):

```
TestRealSystemHostTransactionalOnly  FAIL — real template expects `.fromPort`/`.toPort`,
                                          the test (and the CLI payload) emit `.from`/`.to`
TestRealSystemHostTopicSystemWithContracts  PASS
TestRealSystemHostFieldCollisionFails       PASS
TestRealSystemHostDependencyWhen            PASS
```

Root cause is precise: on **2026-08-14**, both repos did the "connector → port" rename on the same day — templates commit `4c69fd7` (`feat!: rename Connector to Port`, tagged in `v0.4.0`, breaking-change banner: *"payload … component wiring keys connector/from/to → port/fromPort/toPort"*), and CLI commit `ef87c4e` (`refactor: rename topology connector to port`). The coordination was **partial**: `internal/system/blocks.go` reads `fromPort`/`toPort` from scaffold records (correct), but `internal/system/payload.go:60-61` still emits `from`/`to` into the payload. The real template's `{{ .systemClass }}.cs.tmpl:32` does `index $portField .fromPort` and fails with `missingkey=error`.

**So this is plausibly a live production bug**, not just a test smell: `sys create` on a transactional system against template release ≥ v0.4.0 should fail to render. The reason CI is green is exactly the drift mechanism from the analysis — `create_test.go`'s inline fixture copies use `from`/`to` to match the CLI, so fixture and code drifted from the library *together*.

**`internal/deploy` local-template tests** are also red: 3 of 5 fail against the current checkout (`spec.files[7] ... <.binding>: map has no entry` — the deploy payload and the template's `when` conditions have drifted on a `binding` key as well).

This validates recommendation 2 emphatically: had the e2e tests been CI-gated, both drifts would have been caught on the day they happened.

## Gap 4 closed: payload coverage is adequate

`payload_test.go` is exactly the right place for the contract assertions — it already verifies payload shape per component kind, key absence (`port` omitted when absent, `sharedContracts` omitted when none), the facts-only property (`TestBuildPayloadIsFactsOnly` even walks the tree banning field-identifier keys), and empty-list guarantees. The rendered-output derivation assertions in `create_test.go` can be deleted without losing CLI-side coverage. One caveat: `payload_test.go` itself currently encodes `from`/`to` — so it will need updating to `fromPort`/`toPort` as part of fixing the production bug, and `TestBuildPayloadIsFactsOnly`'s banned-key list (`topicField`, `portField`...) was clearly written when the CLI was *sending* those keys — good guard, keep it.

## Where this leaves the plan

Sequencing changes: **fix the payload drift first** (`payload.go` `from`/`to` → `fromPort`/`toPort`, plus the matching test updates), then investigate the deploy `binding` drift — these are user-facing bugs. The fixture-shrink work then proceeds on a green baseline.

Do you want me to:
1. Confirm the transactional failure is live by reproducing `sys create` end-to-end against the local templates checkout, then fix the payload keys (small, focused PR)?
2. Investigate the deploy `binding` drift separately?
3. Then proceed with the original recommendations 1–4?

And per your decision 1(a) — the note for what the template repo is expected to test: field-identifier derivations (kebab/snake → PascalCase), collision errors ("both derive the Topics.cs field …"), the `spec.files`/`when` conditionality per platform, and the dependency `when` expressions. I'll include that note in the work.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(sys): emit fromPort/toPort in the transactional payload

The connector-to-port rename updated the scaffold record keys
(fromPort/toPort) but left the system-host payload emitting from/to.
The template library's system-host (v0.4.0+) reads
{{ index \$portField .fromPort }}, so sys create on a workspace with a
transactional integration failed to render with missingkey=error.

The drift passed CI because the inline fixture in create_test.go
copied the CLI's keys instead of the library's — fixture and code
drifted together. The e2e tests against a real intropy-templates
checkout catch it; they are opt-in and did not run.

- payload.go: transactional wiring keys from/to -> fromPort/toPort
- payload_test.go: assert the new keys; ban the old ones
- create_test.go: align the fixture's system-class template
- real_template_e2e_test.go: payload now matches the library (+gofmt)

Verified: INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR=<checkout> go test -tags e2e
./internal/system/ passes all four TestRealSystemHost tests, including
the previously failing transactional-only case.
EOF
)"
